label: copy phase: re-reading t (or 3) late in the copy, especially right before outputting 3
predicate: (phase == 2) & (((in_tok == tok("t")) & isin(out_tok, [tok("3"), tok("t"), tok("p"), tok("z"), tok("2")])) | ((in_tok == tok("3")) & isin(out_tok, [tok("3"), tok("t")]))) & (recall_idx >= 4)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original tokens or on <DEL>), and only when the fed-back input is t (90% of activation mass) or 3 (9%). It always fires on a repeated token (in_first=0), never on the first time a token appears. Rate rises steeply with position: almost nothing before recall_idx 3, peaks at recall_idx 7-8 (t 14-17), so most mass is in L=8-9 sequences. Within t inputs, the token being output now strongly sets both whether it fires and how strongly: output 3 (the t->3 bigram) gives the top activations (top example w 3 o e e [t] 3 1), followed by t, p, z and 2. For input 3, the output is usually 3 or t. It does not fire on most copy-phase t inputs (only about 8.5% overall), early t inputs, or t followed by other letters, which mostly give weak activations. Dev F1 is about 0.57 with mass recall about 0.78. Precision is limited because many late t->3/t/p/z inputs stay inactive.
